mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate over three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by at least 0.4pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower (p > 0.05) during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE rising by at least 0.4pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% over four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening in monetary policy and accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase of at least 2% in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) over two months signals a robust acceleration in household demand, which boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both rise by at least 2% over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when both PAYEMS and HOUST rise by at least 2% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% combined with a concurrent decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% over three months signals a deepening labor market crisis, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6.5% and PAYEMS falls by more than 1% over three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods where UNRATE exceeds 6.5% and PAYEMS declines by more than 1% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized growth in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 4% for four consecutive quarters signals a strong and sustained demand expansion, which elevates corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in periods where GDPC1 grows above 4% annualized for four consecutive quarters.
